newsitem.title: PERU: Peru Civil Defense denies mudslide disappearances.
newsitem.headline: Peru Civil Defense denies mudslide disappearances.

text.p: Peru's Civil Defence service denied on Tuesday a report that between 150-200 people had disappeared in a mudslide, saying all of them were evacuated from their villages before the landslip.

"By luck, with a cooperation unseen on other occasions, all the entities of Abancay have collaborated and were able to evacuate, with the organisation of the Civil Defence, the 40 families," a Civil Defence official, from the southeastern Andean region of Apurimac, told local television.
The region's deputy governor, Jose Caiyahua, also denied there had been deaths in an early morning landslide in the villages of Ccocha and Pumaranra.
"It's true there was an avalanche, but it's false that there were any deaths. Only houses and trees have fallen down," Caiyahua told Reuters.
Earlier, Luis Barra Pacheco, mayor of Abancay, which is the capital of Apurimac, said between 150 and 200 people were buried in the landslide. He said seven bodies had been recovered so far.
He said an estimated 10.5 million cubic feet (300,000 cubic meters) of mud slid off a nearby mountain. "The mountain buried two communities," he told Reuters by telephone.
